title: Common-resolution formulas for two triple direct-image paths
statement:
Let $X_0\xrightarrow fX_1\xrightarrow gX_2\xrightarrow hX_3$ be morphisms of ringed topoi presented by small sites with sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use their module sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], ordinary unbounded derived categories, and localizations $Q_i:K(\operatorname{Mod}(X_i))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(X_i))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $R_f=Rf_*$, and analogously for composites. Use the normalized natural comparisons $\kappa_{b,a}:R_{ba}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_bR_a$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], and the canonical resolution identifications of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]. All underived composition identifications are the canonical ones, and functor associators are suppressed.
Let $I$ be K-injective on $X_0$ and choose K-injective resolutions $j:f_*I\to J$ on $X_1$, $k:g_*J\to K$ and $t:g_*f_*I\to T$ on $X_2$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then $g_*j$ and $k\circ g_*j$ are quasi-isomorphisms. There is a unique homotopy class of chain maps $u:T\to K$ such that
$$Q_2u=Q_2(k\circ g_*j)\circ(Q_2t)^{-1},\qquad u\circ t\simeq k\circ g_*j.$$
Set $\alpha=(R_h\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}$ and $\beta=(\kappa_{h,g}R_f)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}$. Identify their common source $R_{hgf}(Q_0I)$ with $Q_3(h_*g_*f_*I)$ using $I$, and their common target $R_hR_gR_f(Q_0I)$ with $Q_3(h_*K)$ using $j$ and $k$. In precisely these coordinates their components are
$$\alpha_{Q_0I}=Q_3(h_*u)\circ Q_3(h_*t),\qquad
\beta_{Q_0I}=Q_3(h_*k)\circ Q_3(h_*g_*j).$$
More explicitly, $\kappa_{h,gf}$ is represented by $h_*t$; the map $R_h(\kappa_{g,f,Q_0I})$, using $t$ and $k$ to resolve its source and target, is represented by $h_*u$; $\kappa_{hg,f}$ is represented by $h_*g_*j$; and $\kappa_{h,g}$ at $R_f(Q_0I)$, after the identification induced by $j$, is represented by $h_*k$. The formulas hold for every choice of $j,k,t$ with the canonical resolution transitions. Neither $f_*I$ nor $g_*J$ is assumed K-injective, and no module direct image is assumed to preserve K-injectives.
